title: LongScape: Advancing Long-Horizon Embodied World Models with Context-Aware MoE
claim: Partition a continuous stream into variable-length segments whose boundaries follow semantic activity cues, short for active events and long for subtle ones.
layout: 1 panel, 3 aligned rows, left-to-right, labeled chunk boxes
description: A single horizontal strip with three labeled rows. The top row, 'Chunk length', gives frame counts for four consecutive chunks: 32, 8, 16 and 24 frames. The middle row, 'Chunk split', shows each chunk as a rounded purple box holding stacked robot-manipulation video frames at both ends, with gray dots between them for the omitted frames. The box widths differ with chunk length, and the 8-frame box is the narrowest and has a fainter outline. The bottom row, 'Action-based prior', gives the rule behind each split: 'Right arm's action range exceeds the threshold', 'Right effector state changes', 'Right arm's action range exceeds the threshold', and 'Left arm's action range exceeds the threshold'. The eye goes first to the purple chunk boxes and the real frames inside them.
caption: Action-guided chunk partitioning mechanism. This mechanism leverages embodied actions to partition the video, ensuring each chunk contains a distinct semantic unit. It divides the stream into short segments for active manipulation (e.g., significant movement or end-effector state changes) and longer segments for subtle locomotion dynamics.
abstract: Video-based world models hold significant potential for generating high-quality embodied manipulation data. However, current video generation methods struggle to achieve stable long-horizon generation: classical diffusion-based approaches often suffer from temporal inconsistency and visual drift over multiple rollouts, while autoregressive methods tend to compromise on visual detail. To solve this, we introduce LongScape, a hybrid framework that adaptively combines intra-chunk diffusion denoising with inter-chunk autoregressive causal generation. Our core innovation is an action-guided, variable-length chunking mechanism that partitions video based on the semantic context of robotic actions. This aligns chunk boundaries with robotic interaction events and motion dynamics, enabling the model to flexibly generate diverse dynamics. We further introduce a Context-aware Mixture-of-Experts (CMoE) framework that adaptively activates specialized experts for each chunk during generation to produce high-quality videos with coherent chunk transitions. Extensive experiments on two embodied benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation performance. Notably, LongScape maintains high generation quality and temporal consistency over 1,000-frame rollouts. When used as synthetic training data, LongScape videos lift the success rate of a downstream VLA policy by 9.8 percentage points over real-only training, outperforming augmentation with other long-video generators. Our code is available at: https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/Longscape.
